content:
The ISA goal is funded at plan — worth stating plainly. With £2,850 free cash flow a month and the 7% middle case needing £1,772/mo, you have £1,078/mo to spare against the target. The 7% figure is the moderate middle of the range — roughly the long-run average a broadly diversified portfolio has returned over a horizon like this — an assumption, not a promise, which is why the 4% stress case (£1,805/mo) and 10% upside (£1,738/mo) stay in view. Even at 4%, you're covered. The £8,898 already saved is doing real work here: compounding on that existing pot means the monthly lift needed is far lower than a flat split would suggest.

One note on the data: the most recent transaction here is from 2026-03-28, so these observations are as of that date, not today.

**Subscriptions** are running £126/month across the window. With no Value Map yet to tell me which of those you'd defend, that's the one category where there's clear room to move without touching anything structural.

Trimming £31/month from subscriptions won't shift the goal date — the math is already working — but it tightens the floor and edges you toward covering the 4% stress case with even more headroom. That's the next clean move.

[CTA:cut_lever]Trim £31 from subscriptions[/CTA]

— C.
